topic: Notochord, Dorsal Hollow Nerve Cord, Urochordata & Cephalochordata
quickSummary: Chordates are defined by a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, and post-anal tail. Urochordates possess notochords only in larval tails (retrogressive metamorphosis), while Cephalochordates retain a head-to-tail notochord throughout life.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Protochordates are acraniates: Urochordata has notochord only in larval tail (*Ascidia*); Cephalochordata has persistent notochord from snout to tail (*Branchiostoma*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Structural Comparison: Chordates vs. Non-Chordates
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Structural Comparison: Chordates vs. Non-Chordates
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Diagnostic Trait | Phylum Chordata | Non-Chordates (Invertebrates) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Notochord** | Present at some stage of life cycle | **Absent** entirely |
| **Central Nervous System** | **Dorsal**, **Hollow**, Single | **Ventral**, **Solid**, Double (paired nerve cords with ganglia) |
| **Pharyngeal Gill Slits** | Present at some embryonic/adult stage | **Absent** |
| **Heart Location** | **Ventral** to alimentary canal | **Dorsal** or lateral (if present) |
| **Post-Anal Tail** | Present at some stage | **Absent** (anus is terminal) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Subphylum Urochordata & 5.3 Subphylum Cephalochordata
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Subphylum Urochordata & 5.3 Subphylum Cephalochordata
conceptBreakdown.content:
### Subphylum Urochordata (Tunicata)
• **Notochord Distribution**: Notochord and nerve cord are present **ONLY in the free-swimming larval tail**.
• **Retrogressive Metamorphosis**: The active, bilaterally symmetrical, tadpole larva undergoes degenerative metamorphosis into a sessile, bag-like adult that loses its notochord, nerve cord, and tail.
• **Tunicin Coat**: Body enclosed in a protective tunic composed of **Tunicin** (chemically similar to plant cellulose).
• **Key Taxa**: *Ascidia*, *Salpa*, *Doliolum*.

### Subphylum Cephalochordata
• **Persistent Notochord**: Notochord extends from the extreme anterior rostrum/head to the tail ($100\%$ of body length) and **persists throughout life**.
• **Body Plan**: Translucent, fish-like, ciliary filter-feeding marine organisms with myotomes.
• **Key Taxa**: *Branchiostoma* (*Amphioxus* / Lancelet).
